The MILP solver enforces lineup constraints such as salary caps, overlap limits, and archetype rules while avoiding sub-floor traps. The Student-$t$ engine simulates correlated player performance under heavy-tailed distributions, capturing tail risk. These primitives interlock through a two-stage pipeline where Stage 1 generates stochastic game states, Stage 2 curates valid players, and Stage 3 applies optimized strategies. Dualities emerge between deterministic MILP constraints and probabilistic simulation outcomes. Failure modes include constraint violation in MILP or insufficient simulation coverage in Student-$t$. The system avoids overfitting by enforcing structural accuracy gates (G1–G5) that filter out invalid lineups.
